methodology.how: argparse --drop at :579 -> main() :594-596 'if args.drop: drop_cse_table(catalog, args.table); return 0' -> :348 drop_cse_table -> :353 catalog.drop_table((NAMESPACE, table)). NOT an append. The branch returns immediately and ⛔ --dry-run is NOT consulted on it.
declared_opinions: ⛔ --dry-run does not gate this branch. On PATH A the flag is threaded to ingest_jsonl (:584 -> :602); on PATH B main() calls drop_cse_table and returns 0 before any dry-run test. An operator who reaches for --dry-run as a safety habit gets it on one path of this file and not the other.

The protection is a SELF-protection, not a namespace membership check -- it is keyed to this module's own table name, so it bounds the path against harming its own log and not against harming a sibling's.
A destructive path sharing one unconstrained --table arg with an append path means the same typo has two very different consequences depending on which flag accompanies it.

methodology.evidence: SOURCE READ @76c58923ac. ⛔ I NEARLY OVERSTATED THIS ROW AND THE CHECK THAT STOPPED IT IS WORTH THE SPACE: from the main() dispatch alone (:594-596) PATH B reads as unbounded AND ungated, which is an alarming and wrong finding. Reading the FUNCTION shows :350-352 -- 'if table == CSE_TABLE: raise ValueError(REFUSED: cse is the real append-only C0 log -- never dropped here)'. The guard exists, does exactly what its docstring says, and protects the C0 log. The defensible version is weaker than the one I could have shipped: the guard is keyed to this module's OWN table name, so --table cse is refused and any other globgrph table name is not reached by it. Recorded as a MEASURED PROPERTY of the bound, NOT as a defect claim -- COX3-AC8 QUALIFY-DO-NOT-FIX binds this lane and globgrph is read-only to it.

cadence.actual_trigger: NONE-FOUND, and the negative is a real one. The ONLY caller of drop_cse_table in the swept tree is cse_store.py:595 itself -- the CLI dispatch. Sweep: grep for drop_cse_table( across infra/ and org/, excluding the definition, returned exactly one hit. No ECS task definition invokes cse_store.py at all (7 of 7 ACTIVE families read). So this path executes only when a human types --drop.
cadence.evidence: TWO-PLANE SWEEP, client-side counted (never --query length on a paginated list -- events list-rules returned 100 then 37 as PAGE counts): events=137, scheduler=18. POSITIVE CONTROL FIRED and it caught a broken sweep of mine: my first container-command loop printed only globgrph-trino (a multi-line shell command swallowed the rest) and my second returned blank for 6 of 7 families; the control -- describe-task-definition on globgrph-cse-producer -> 'python /app/cse_producers_nightly.py' -- proved both were instrument failures rather than absences. The values here come from the form the control validated. 7 ACTIVE task-definition families, all read. A destructive path with no trigger is the correct and expected shape; recording it as MEASURED rather than assumed, because 'nothing triggers the dangerous thing' is exactly the claim that should not be taken on faith.

persistence.evidence: ⛔ mutation_policy IS RECORDED AS 'replaceable' AND THAT IS A FLOOR-FIT, NOT AN ACCURATE VALUE. The v2 enum is [editable, append_only, replaceable, immutable, not_applicable] and it has NO DESTRUCTIVE MEMBER; this path DROPS the table. I picked the closest legal value and am declaring the mismatch here rather than letting a legal-looking value imply the enum covered this case. Note the contrast in the contract itself: authority_role carries x-enum-definitions AND an x-rule24 block, mutation_policy carries neither -- the un-disciplined enum is the one with the uncovered member (Rule 24 postulate (i)). Routed separately; NOT amended here. The measured fact: drop MEASURED at :353 catalog.drop_table((NAMESPACE, table)). This is the row that made the split necessary: PATH A's mutation_policy is append-only and PATH B's is destructive, and no single card can carry both honestly.
